result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend the same openly licensed families (Atkinson Hyperlegible Next and Source Serif 4), self-hosted WOFF2 files, font-display: swap, and fallback stacks that end in sans-serif. A wins narrowly because it states the licensing plainly and its device checks include a test print on a cheap printer. B hedges on a license that is in fact the SIL Open Font License and leaves out a print test, though it is clearer that one family can serve both web and print and it gives ready-to-use CSS. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers pick openly licensed faces (Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, Source Serif 4), recommend self-hosting WOFF2 with font-display: swap, and use fallback stacks that end in sans-serif. B covers print and web in separate sections and adds a test print on a cheap printer to the real-device checks, saying that test matters more than any recommendation. A gives ready-to-use CSS and clearly says one family can serve both web and print, but its testing advice leaves out the print check.
